title: A Normal Debate? - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Alex Tabarrok points to an AI-generated video diss track attacking Narayanan and Kapoor's 'AI as Normal Technology' thesis, and Kapoor's own AI-made reply, arguing the near-fully AI-produced creative output itself undercuts claims that AI is normal or uncreative.

insights.claim: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor argue 'AI is normal technology' — a description, prediction and prescription holding that AI is a tool humans can and should stay in control of without drastic policy interventions or technical breakthroughs.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: A prominent 'slow-diffusion' framing that implies gradual rather than discontinuous economic impact from AI.
insights.quote: We view AI as a tool that we can and should remain in control of, and we argue that this goal does not require drastic policy interventions or technical breakthroughs.

insights.claim: Narayanan and Kapoor contend that viewing AI as humanlike intelligence is neither accurate nor useful for understanding its societal impacts, now or in their vision of the future.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Underpins skepticism of AGI-driven investment narratives.

insights.claim: An almost entirely AI-generated video diss track — script, music and lyrics — responded to the 'AI as Normal Technology' thesis, and Kapoor answered with his own diss track; Tabarrok calls both great.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Illustrates how cheap high-quality AI media production has become.
insights.quote: Keep in mind that this is almost entirely AI, the script, the music, the lyrics everything.
insights.locator: Both of these are good, great

themes.theme: Implied rebuttal: AI is not normal

insights.claim: Tabarrok implies the episode itself refutes the 'normal technology' framing: it seems like just yesterday people said AI could never be creative, and this does not look like a normal debate regardless of who won.
insights.speaker: Alex Tabarrok
insights.so_what: Tabarrok leans toward the view that AI's capability shift is discontinuous, favoring faster-impact scenarios.
insights.quote: It seems like just yesterday when people said AI could never be creative.
insights.locator: Both of these are good, great
